bottom_line: In patients with drug-eluting stents, continued thienopyridine plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin from 12 to 30 months reduced stent thrombosis (hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.48]).
implications: These data support that, during months 12–30 after enrollment, continuing thienopyridine (with aspirin) lowers Kaplan–Meier event rates of stent thrombosis (0.4% vs. 1.4%) and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (4.3% vs. 5.9%) versus placebo (with aspirin), but increases moderate or severe bleeding (2.5% vs. 1.6%). The document also reports an elevated risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction during the 3 months after thienopyridine discontinuation in both groups, and does not establish effects for other stent types or non-thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitors.

major_points.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled comparison of continuing thienopyridine vs placebo for 18 additional months after 12 months of open-label thienopyridine plus aspirin; aspirin continued in all patients.
major_points.quote: After 12 months of treatment with a thienopyridine drug (clopidogrel or prasugrel) and aspirin, patients were randomly assigned to continue receiving thienopyridine treatment or to receive placebo for another 18 months; all patients continued receiving aspirin.

major_points.text: Coprimary efficacy endpoints were stent thrombosis and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) from 12 to 30 months.
major_points.quote: The coprimary efficacy end points were stent thrombosis and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (a compos- ite of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) during the period from 12 to 30 months.

major_points.text: Continued thienopyridine reduced major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events vs placebo during months 12–30.
Bleeding (GUSTO moderate or severe) was higher with continued thienopyridine vs placebo during months 12–30.
An elevated risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction was observed in both groups during the 3 months after stopping thienopyridine.
major_points.quote: An elevated risk of stent thrombo- sis and myocardial infarction was observed in both groups during the 3 months after discontinuation of thienopyridine treatment.

absolute_effects.text: Major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events: 4.3% vs 5.9%.
GUSTO severe or moderate bleeding: 2.5% vs 1.6% (difference 1.0 percentage points [0.4 to 1.5]).

subgroups.text: Effect of treatment was assessed in subgroups defined by 14 prespecified baseline factors.
subgroups.quote: We also assessed the consistency of the effect of treatment on the primary end points in subgroups defined accord- ing to 14 prespecified factors assessed at baseline.

subgroups.text: The effect of continued thienopyridine vs placebo was consistent across most subgroups.
subgroups.quote: The effect of continued thienopyridine therapy versus placebo on the rates of the primary end points and on the rate of myocardial infarction was consistent across most subgroups

harms.text: Moderate or severe bleeding (GUSTO) was higher with continued thienopyridine vs placebo.
All-cause mortality was 2.0% with continued thienopyridine vs 1.5% with placebo during months 12–30.
Study drug discontinuation at 30 months did not differ significantly between groups.
harms.quote: The rates of discon- tinuation of the study drug did not differ sig- nificantly at 30 months between the group that continued thienopyridine therapy and the group that received placebo (21.4% and 20.3%, respec- tively; P = 0.18).

analysis_methods.text: Controlled two-sided family-wise error rate of 0.05 across two coprimary endpoints using Hochberg–Benjamini method.
analysis_methods.quote: We controlled the two-sided family-wise error rate of 0.05 across the two coprimary end points using the Hochberg–Benjamini method.

analysis_methods.text: Primary analyses used the intention-to-treat population including all randomized patients treated with drug-eluting stents.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary analyses of major adverse car- diovascular and cerebrovascular events and stent thrombosis were performed on data from all pa- tients who underwent randomization and were treated with drug-eluting stents (the intention-to- treat population).

analysis_methods.text: With a sample of 9800 drug-eluting-stent patients undergoing randomization, the study would have at least 85% power for the superiority analysis under specified assumptions.
analysis_methods.quote: we calculated that with a sample of 9800 patients undergoing randomization and receiv- ing drug-eluting stents, the study would have at least 85% power for the superiority analysis.

analysis_methods.text: For bleeding noninferiority, a sample size of 9960 provided 80% power (one-sided alpha 0.025) with a 0.8% margin under stated assumptions.
analysis_methods.quote: we calculated that a sample size of 9960 patients would give the study 80% power to detect noninferiority.

analysis_methods.text: Missing data handled with multiple-imputation logistic-regression modeling (50 imputations).
